chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan: The correct way of understanding this report is that he is liable for what the beast tramples with its forelegs and hind legs when he is stationary, according to what we have presented in the report of al-'Ala' ibn al-Fudayl from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام. But if he is moving, then nothing is upon him for what it tramples with its feet, according to what we have previously presented in all the reports.

key_terms.وَاقِفًا: being stationary rather than in motion
key_terms.يَضْمَنُ: is held legally liable or responsible for compensation
key_terms.ٱلْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports used as evidence
key_terms.ٱلْوَجْهُ: the proper interpretive approach or legal explanation

ai.seo_question: When is a rider liable for damage caused by an animal trampling someone or something?
ai.summary: This passage presents a juristic clarification by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan on how to reconcile reports concerning liability for damage caused by a ridden animal. The ruling distinguishes between the rider being stationary, in which case liability applies, and being in motion, in which case liability does not apply for what the animal tramples with its feet.
